questions.prompt: Why is C++ considered multi-paradigm rather than pure OOP?
questions.answerKey: C++ supports procedural programming (`main()`, free functions), primitive non-object types (`int`), generic programming (templates), and functional lambdas alongside OOP.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between Encapsulation and Abstraction with a real-life example.
questions.answerKey: **Encapsulation:** bundling data + methods and hiding raw state (`private balance_`) to protect invariants. **Abstraction:** exposing *what* an object does while hiding *how* (dashboard pedals vs engine internals).

questions.prompt: Why is `sizeof(EmptyClass)` equal to 1 byte instead of 0?
questions.answerKey: So two distinct objects in an array `Empty arr[2];` have distinct addresses (`&arr[0] != &arr[1]`). (Exception: EBO when inherited.)

questions.prompt: What is the exact difference between a `struct` and a `class` in C++?
questions.answerKey: Only default member access (`public` in `struct`, `private` in `class`) and default inheritance mode (`public` in `struct`, `private` in `class`).

questions.prompt: Can one `Student` object access `private` members of another `Student` object inside a member method? Why?
questions.answerKey: **Yes.** Access control in C++ is class-based, not object-based—needed for copy constructors and `operator==`.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `T b = a;` and `b = a;`?
questions.answerKey: `T b = a;` calls **Copy Constructor** (new object born); `b = a;` calls **Copy Assignment Operator** (`b` already exists).

questions.prompt: Why can't a constructor be `virtual` or `static`?
questions.answerKey: Virtual dispatch needs `vptr` (which the constructor itself sets up); `static` has no `this` pointer to initialize.

questions.prompt: Explain `this` pointer type inside a normal vs `const` member function.
questions.answerKey: Normal: `T* const`. `const` method: `const T* const`.

questions.prompt: Why can't a `static` member function be marked `const`?
questions.answerKey: `const` qualifies the hidden `this` pointer; `static` functions have no `this` pointer.

questions.prompt: Explain how you would design a **Singleton Logger** in C++17 safely (thread-safe, no memory leak, non-copyable).

questions.prompt: Why must the copy constructor take `const T&` instead of `T` by value?
questions.answerKey: Pass-by-value parameter `T` would invoke the copy constructor itself -> infinite recursion (rejected at compile time).

questions.prompt: What two bugs happen when you shallow-copy a class owning a raw `int*`?
questions.answerKey: Aliasing mutation + Double-free UB on destruction (plus memory leak on assignment).

questions.prompt: Why should `operator=` check `if (this == &rhs)` AND return `*this` by reference?
questions.answerKey: `this == &rhs` stops deleting own buffer on `a = a;`; returning `T&` enables chaining `a = b = c;` without temporary copies.

questions.prompt: Explain why `delete[] data_` should come **after** allocating the new buffer inside `operator=`.
questions.answerKey: Strong exception safety: if `new[]` throws `std::bad_alloc`, old `data_` isn't dangling!

questions.prompt: What does C++17 Guaranteed Copy Elision do on `Box b = makeBox();`?
questions.answerKey: Constructs `makeBox()`'s return prvalue directly in `b`'s memory—zero copy/move calls!

questions.prompt: Compare `public`, `protected`, and `private` inheritance in one sentence each.
questions.answerKey: `public` = "is-a" (keeps public/protected); `protected` = caps public to protected; `private` = "implemented-in-terms-of" (caps public/protected to private, hides upcast).

questions.prompt: Explain **Function Hiding (Name Hiding)** and how `using Base::fn;` fixes it.
questions.answerKey: Defining `Derived::fn(double)` hides *all* `Base::fn` overloads; `using Base::fn;` pulls them into `Derived`'s overload set.

questions.prompt: Why can't two functions overload solely by return type?
questions.answerKey: Callers can ignore return values (`fn(5);`), making resolution impossible.

questions.prompt: What is the exact construction order in `class C : public B, public A { Member m; };`?

questions.prompt: What are the 3 mandatory conditions for runtime polymorphism in C++?
questions.answerKey: Public inheritance, `virtual` function in Base overridden in Derived, called via `Base*` or `Base&`.

questions.prompt: Explain `vptr` and `vtable`—how many of each exist in memory?
questions.answerKey: **One `vtable` per polymorphic class**; **one `vptr` per object**.

questions.prompt: Why is deleting a `Derived` object via `Base*` without a `virtual` destructor Undefined Behavior?
questions.answerKey: C++ standard explicitly marks `delete basePtr` with non-virtual `~Base()` as **Undefined Behavior** (derived destructor/cleanup skipped, allocator metadata mismatch).

questions.prompt: What is **Object Slicing**, and how does passing by `const Base&` stop it?
questions.answerKey: Copying `Derived` by value into `Base` drops derived data and resets `vptr` to `Base`; `const Base&` binds directly without copying.

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't you override default parameter values on a `virtual` function?
questions.answerKey: Default args are statically bound using pointer type (`Base*`), while function body is dynamically bound (`Derived::fn`) -> mismatched combo!

title: Diamond Problem, Multiple Inheritance & C++17 `inline static`

questions.prompt: Explain the Diamond Problem and how `virtual` inheritance solves it.
questions.answerKey: Duplicate copies of grand-base `A` cause ambiguity and wasted memory; `virtual public A` on `B` and `C` merges `A` into one shared subobject.

questions.prompt: In virtual inheritance (`A -> B, C -> D`), which constructor initializes `A`?
questions.answerKey: Always the **most-derived class (`D`)**; `B`/`C`'s calls to `A(...)` are ignored when constructing `D`.

questions.prompt: Why does `Base1* p1 = &d;` vs `Base2* p2 = &d;` give different raw memory addresses in multiple inheritance?
questions.answerKey: `B2` lives at a non-zero byte offset after `B1` inside `Derived`; compiler adds `+offset` during `Derived* -> Base2*`.

questions.prompt: Why did C++17 introduce `inline static` data members, and what does `inline` mean on a variable?
questions.answerKey: Allows defining/initializing any `static` member (including mutable and `std::string`) inside headers; `inline` tells linker to merge duplicate definitions across TUs into one variable.

questions.prompt: Are `static constexpr` members implicitly `inline` in C++17? Why does that matter when taking `&Class::CONST`?
questions.answerKey: **Yes** (`static constexpr` is implicitly `inline` in C++17, so taking `&Class::CONST` needs no out-of-class definition).

title: Rule of 3, Rule of 5, Rule of 0 & Memory Internals

questions.prompt: State the Rule of 3, Rule of 5, and Rule of 0, and explain why Rule of 0 is preferred in C++17.
questions.answerKey: Rule of 3 (`~T`, copy ctor, copy assign); Rule of 5 (+ move ctor, move assign); Rule of 0 (compose RAII types, write none). Rule of 0 eliminates leaks and boilerplate.

questions.prompt: What happens to implicit move operations if you write `~MyClass() = default;` in a non-polymorphic class?
questions.answerKey: Suppresses implicit generation of move constructor and move assignment!

questions.prompt: Why must move constructors and move assignment operators be marked `noexcept`?
questions.answerKey: Otherwise `std::vector` falls back to slow copying during reallocation to maintain strong exception safety.

questions.prompt: What happens if you call `std::move` on a `const` object?
questions.answerKey: `std::move(constObj)` produces `const T&&`, which cannot bind to `T&&` -> silently calls the **Copy Constructor**!

questions.prompt: Explain the **Empty Base Optimization (EBO)** and why `sizeof(Derived)` can be smaller than `sizeof(Empty) + sizeof(int)`.
questions.answerKey: Compiler gives an empty base class 0 bytes inside `Derived` (`sizeof(Derived) == sizeof(int)`).

title: Final Boss — Hard Internals, Edge Cases & System Design

questions.prompt: Explain the **Static Initialization Order Fiasco (SIOF)** and why `inline static` alone does not fix cross-TU initialization order.
questions.answerKey: `inline static` merges duplicate definitions across `.cpp` files (fixes ODR), **not** cross-TU initialization order! Use Meyers' Singleton (`static T& instance()`) for order-dependent globals.

questions.prompt: Explain the **PIMPL idiom** and why `~Widget()` must be defined in `.cpp` when using `std::unique_ptr<Impl>`.
questions.answerKey: `std::unique_ptr<Impl>`'s default deleter calls `delete pImpl_`, requiring `Impl` to be a complete type where `~Widget()` is instantiated—so define `~Widget() = default;` in `.cpp` after `struct Impl`.

questions.prompt: Compare `static_cast`, `dynamic_cast`, and `reinterpret_cast` in a multiple/virtual inheritance hierarchy.
questions.answerKey: `static_cast` adjusts offsets statically (cannot downcast from `virtual` base); `dynamic_cast` uses RTTI safely at runtime (handles `virtual` bases); `reinterpret_cast` skips offset adjustments (dangerous across MI!).

questions.prompt: Explain the **Non-Virtual Interface (NVI)** idiom and why `private virtual` is legal and useful.
questions.answerKey: Public non-virtual method enforces pre/post-conditions and calls `private virtual` hooks overridden by subclasses.

questions.prompt: How does the **Passkey Idiom** give finer-grained access control than `friend class`?
questions.answerKey: Nested `class Key { Key() = default; friend class Trusted; };` lets `Trusted` call *only* the gated method without touching private fields.
